deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): this is the genus-3 (plane quartic) theory. The 28 'Abel'sche Functionen' are square roots √x of the 28 bitangent linear forms, i.e. the 28 odd theta characteristics. The 378 pairs fall into 63 'Gruppen' (modern: Steiner complexes) of 6 pairs each, indexed by the 63 nonzero characteristics. For two pairs √(xy), √(zt) of one group the quartic can be written F = f^2 - xyzt = 0. Equation (8) says any product √(pq) of a group is a linear combination of two others: √(pq) = √(zt) + α√(xy). The previous page ends with the claim that three known pairs of a group determine the rest by a cubic, and from them all 28 bitangents with their characteristics. This page begins that computation.

Setup. Let x·ξ, y·η, z·ζ be three pairs of one group. Here x, y, z are independent linear forms (projective coordinates), and ξ, η, ζ are given linear forms in x, y, z. The manuscript corrects 'von ξηζ' to 'von x,y,z'. Rescaling the forms by constants turns (8) into
(9) √(xξ) + √(yη) + √(zζ) = 0.
Squaring gives zζ = xξ + yη + 2√(xξ·yη), so
(10) 4·xξ·yη = (zζ - xξ - yη)^2.
(11) Set f = zζ - xξ - yη. The quartic is then f^2 - 4xξyη = 0.

Strategy. Finding all pairs of the group {xξ, yη, ...} needs a quartic ('biquadratische') equation with one root (the pair zζ) already known. Riemann instead uses the group of the pair xη, which also contains yξ, since (xη)(yξ) = (xξ)(yη). Equation (10) then reads f^2 - 4·(xη)(yξ) = 0, which is the normal form of the quartic for this second group.

Let pq be a further unknown pair of the group of xη. By the analogue of (7) on the previous page, yξ·pq must be a perfect square:
(12) 4yξ·pq = φ^2, with φ = f ± 2λ·yξ (the manuscript writes +), λ an unknown constant.
Using (10)/(11) the manuscript writes
φ^2 = 4λyξ (xξ + yη - zζ + xη/λ + λyξ).
[My check: this holds exactly for φ = f - 2λyξ, since (f - 2λyξ)^2 = 4yξ(xη - λf + λ^2 yξ). With φ = f + 2λyξ as written one gets the same formula with λ replaced by -λ.]
Dropping the factor λ:
pq = xξ + yη - zζ + xη/λ + λyξ = (ξ + η/λ)(x + λy) - zζ.

Next, where x + λy = 0 and z = 0 (a single point of the plane), pq vanishes. So one factor, say p, vanishes there. Normalizing p:
(13) p = x + λy + μz, with μ unknown.
Substituting x + λy = p - μz:
pq = p(ξ + η/λ) - μz(ξ + η/λ + ζ/μ).
Hence p divides μz(ξ + η/λ + ζ/μ). Since p is not proportional to z, the linear form ξ + η/λ + ζ/μ is a constant multiple of p. Write the constant as -a^2:
(14) ξ + η/λ + ζ/μ = -a^2·p.
[Mine: then q = ξ + η/λ + a^2 μ z.]
Inserting (13) and dividing by a:
(15) a x + aλ y + aμ z + ξ/a + η/(λa) + ζ/(μa) = 0.

This is a linear relation among x, y, z, ξ, η, ζ with parameters (a, λ, μ). Each solution yields a bitangent p = x + λy + μz of the group of xη. Margin note: 'Und hieraus weiter.'

This is the derivation leading to Riemann's normal form of the 28 bitangents. In that form ξ, η, ζ are fixed by x + y + z + ξ + η + ζ = 0 and two relations of type (15), a_i x + b_i y + c_i z + ξ/a_i + η/b_i + ζ/c_i = 0.
errors: Sign inconsistency: with φ = f + 2λyξ and f = zζ - xξ - yη as defined in (11), φ^2 = 4λyξ(zζ - xξ - yη + xη/λ + λyξ), not 4λyξ(xξ + yη - zζ + xη/λ + λyξ). The written formula is correct for φ = f - 2λyξ, i.e. after λ -> -λ. Since λ is an undetermined constant, this is harmless for the rest of the derivation.

The step 'pq vanishes where x + λy = 0, z = 0, so one factor vanishes there' is valid because pq is a product of two linear forms. The normalisation of p's coefficient of x to 1 is tacit; it also needs p not to be proportional to x + λy alone, which is implicitly assumed.

The divisibility step behind (14) is correct: p | μz·L with p not proportional to z (and μ ≠ 0) forces L ∝ p. Writing the constant as -a^2 is a convenience for the symmetric form (15), and the division by a assumes a ≠ 0. No genuine mathematical error.

results.what: Writing the plane quartic, via three pairs of bitangents from one Steiner complex, as √(xξ) + √(yη) + √(zζ) = 0, equivalently (zζ - xξ - yη)^2 = 4xξyη
results.modern_name: Riemann's (Hesse–Riemann) normal form of a plane quartic via bitangents / Steiner complexes
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures; posthumous 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3', Werke 1876, ed. Weber), building on Hesse, Steiner (1855) and Aronhold (1864)

results.what: Using the 'crossed' group of xη (containing yξ) to find further bitangents p = x + λy + μz satisfying the linear relation a x + aλ y + aμ z + ξ/a + η/(λa) + ζ/(μa) = 0
results.modern_name: Riemann's parametrisation of the 28 bitangents (Riemann's normal form / Aronhold-type system with reciprocal coefficients)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published posthumously); elaborated by H. Weber, Theorie der Abelschen Functionen vom Geschlecht 3 (1876)

results.what: Classification of the 378 pairs of the 28 odd characteristics into 63 groups of 6 pairs with equal characteristic sum (context from previous page)
results.modern_name: Steiner complexes / syzygetic structure of bitangents of a quartic
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner 1855, Hesse 1855; characteristic-theoretic version Riemann, Weber

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard derivation of Riemann's normal form of the bitangents of a plane quartic, which is known and published under Riemann's name (Werke, Weber 1876). The page is a draft of that known material. The only non-cosmetic detail is a harmless sign slip in the constant λ.
